claim: The compatibility guard suppresses ExcludeFromCodeCoverage on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework even though ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available on those targets (including .NET Framework 4.0 and later). Consequently, generated code on supported targets compiled with NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK is not decorated, contrary to the requirement that all generated code be excluded except where the attribute must be conditionally omitted because it does not exist.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageTargetFrameworkTests.GeneratedTypes_RemainExcludedWhenTargetFrameworkSymbolsAreDefined. The test independently verifies that the attribute compiles against netstandard2.0, then inspects active generated declarations with NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK defined; it fails on head because the directives remove the attribute.

claim: Defining NETFRAMEWORK strips ExcludeFromCodeCoverage from every generated formatter and resolver, although the attribute exists on supported modern .NET Framework targets. Consequently, code generated for .NET Framework remains included in coverage, contrary to the requirement that all generated code be decorated; conditional omission is only needed where the attribute is unavailable.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageReceiptTests.NetFrameworkGeneratedTypesStillGetCoverageExclusion. It runs the generator with NETFRAMEWORK defined and asserts that the compiled generated resolver has ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute; the current guard makes the assertion fail.

claim: A consumer that already applied [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] to its partial generated resolver now gets a second copy from ResolverTemplate. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute does not allow multiple attributes, and attributes from partial declarations are combined, so previously valid source fails with CS0579 instead of compiling.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageReceiptTests.UserAttributedResolverDoesNotProduceDuplicateAttribute. It compiles a partial [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] that already has [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage], with the generated attribute active, and asserts that no CS0579 diagnostic is produced.

claim: The tests only require at least one attribute per generated file, so removing ExcludeFromCodeCoverage from an inner generated resolver type would go unnoticed. ResolverTemplate emits separate attributes for FormatterCache<T> and the GetFormatterHelper class, and CompositeResolverTemplate has the same per-file blind spot for FormatterCache<T>; deleting either attribute while retaining the resolver's outer attribute leaves every new assertion passing.

claim: The target-framework compatibility acceptance criterion is checked only by searching for preprocessor strings; the generated compilation is never compiled for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework, or even checked for diagnostics on the default target. Thus syntactically broken generated output could satisfy all three tests.

receipt_plan.detail: Extend RunGeneratorAsync's callers to inspect the compilation returned by RunGeneratorsAndUpdateCompilation, and add compilation cases using netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework reference assemblies with the corresponding preprocessor symbols. Assert no errors both when the guard excludes the attribute and when it is active; the current test at line 101 would not detect generated syntax that fails either compilation.
